samples.summary: New gate 1b makes every workflow-touching managed PR (including this branch) permanently un-promotable, with no page and an unbounded per-push panel cost
samples.evidence:
mark-ready.mjs:210 now adds `ciDefinitionGate` to the gate list, so any PR whose file list touches `.github/workflows/**` exits 1 forever. Consumers that were written before this gate existed do not account for that terminal state:
- `.github/workflows/agent-loop.yml:166` tells a maintainer opting a human PR in: "🔁 Loop enabled … On green CI the review panel runs and can promote it" — false for exactly the population gate 1b was added for (`agent:managed` human PRs, the only ones allowed to push workflows).
- `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1263` posts "Panel approved — the ready gate promotes once CI is green."
- The promote job's exit-1 branch (`agent-review-panel.yml:1541`) records `gates-unsatisfied`, which the loop-status note at line 1577 renders generically and which **does not page**; `stalled` (line 2322) only fires on `failure`, not on a gate saying no.
- `MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS` bounds the FIXER only (see the comment at agent-review-panel.yml:135-137: "a PR that has already been paged still re-runs the whole panel on every CI-green push"), and with all lenses green no round is ever counted — so each subsequent green CI push re-runs the ~$12 panel indefinitely on a PR that can never converge.
This is not hypothetical for this branch: the patch header in docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-trigger-shape.patch states the `.github/workflows/**` commits on this branch were pushed by a maintainer, so this PR itself now fails its own new gate.
Fix belongs on the new gate (or on the promote job's reporting): name gate 1b explicitly in the loop-status note / hand-off so a human is told to flip it, and correct the two "can promote it" messages.

samples.summary: Design doc still carries the pre-gate-1b paragraph, now contradicting the gate 1b section 50 lines above it
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:1956-1963 ("**What gate 1 does NOT prove.**") still states the contract this delta replaced — "Gate 1 therefore means 'a separate actor reports CI green for this SHA', not 'main's CI definition passed'; closing that needs the run's workflow content compared against the base branch" — while lines 1905-1921 in the same file now describe gate 1b closing exactly that gap by reading the PR's file list. mark-ready.mjs's own header comment was updated in this delta; this doc paragraph is the copy that was left behind. A reader reaching 1956 first will conclude the gate does not exist.

samples.summary: Design doc's only description of the trigger-shape canary points at a staged .patch that the patch itself instructs the applier to delete
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:1941-1944 says the canary "is STAGED, NOT LANDED — `docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-trigger-shape.patch` holds the job and its `checks.test.mjs` pin". The new patch file's own header says "Delete this file in the same commit that applies it." The moment a maintainer follows that instruction the doc paragraph becomes both wrong (the canary IS landed) and a dangling backticked reference. It will not be caught mechanically: scripts/verify-entropy.mjs's VALID_EXTENSIONS (line 11-26) has no `.patch`, so the backtick-path check skips it. The doc hunk that must land with the apply should be named in the patch's "BOTH HUNKS LAND TOGETHER" note.

samples.summary: Panel gate comment still describes mark-ready deriving its CI gate from the run path
samples.evidence: agent-review-panel.yml:160-162 says "mark-ready re-derives its own gate from the path (see checks.mjs CI_WORKFLOW_PATH), so promotion was never at risk". mark-ready.mjs no longer derives anything from a run path — gate 1 scopes server-side via `/actions/workflows/${CI_WORKFLOW_FILE}/runs` (mark-ready.mjs:156-159), and checks.test.mjs:544-548 now forbids any JS-side path parsing in that file. The comment describes the exact mechanism the suite bans, so a future editor reading it may reintroduce path matching.

samples.summary: The staged trigger-shape canary lands in the `noop` concurrency group with cancel-in-progress, so its red run can be cancelled away
samples.evidence: The canary in the staged patch fires when `workflow_run.path != '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` — precisely the condition that makes the workflow-level concurrency suffix at agent-review-panel.yml:117 evaluate to `noop`, with `cancel-in-progress: true` (line 118). If the payload field ever goes empty (the canary's headline scenario), EVERY CI run's `requested` and `completed` events map to the same `noop` group for the same head branch, so each later event cancels the in-flight canary. A cancelled run is not the failed run the canary promises (`stalled` at line 2322 deliberately relies on that distinction). The canary body is a few seconds long so this is a narrow window, but the group it is placed in is the one built for runs whose cancellation "costs nothing".

samples.summary: The staged patch pins a fragile context in checks.test.mjs and will stop applying if the branch touches that file again
samples.evidence: The second hunk targets `scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs` at `@@ -216,6 +216,24 @@` with blob index 108157aa9 and six lines of context inside the concurrency-partition block (checks.test.mjs:213-219). Review rounds on this branch routinely edit checks.test.mjs (this PR already has), and any edit near line 216 makes `git apply` reject the hunk — leaving the maintainer with the workflow half applied and the pin missing, which is the exact split the patch header warns must not happen. Anchoring the instruction on `git apply --3way` (or keeping the pin in a file the branch does not otherwise touch) would remove the trap.

samples.summary: Gate 1b's prefix list does not cover the other branch-supplied inputs a `pull_request` CI run executes
samples.evidence: CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES (mark-ready.mjs:175) is `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/` — and `.github/actions/` does not exist in this repo (glob `.github/actions/**` returns nothing). ci.yml executes branch-supplied `package.json` scripts, vitest/jest configs and `scripts/**` from the merge ref, so a branch can still hand gate 1 a green run with no tests in it without touching either prefix. The hand-off comment this delta rewords (mark-ready.mjs:320-322) tells the human reviewer "that run executed the CI file on `main`", which is literally true but reads as a stronger claim than the gate makes. Worth either narrowing the wording or recording the residual gap where the old "What this does NOT guarantee" note used to sit.

verdict.reason: Gate 1b and both quoted message strings do exist, but the consequences graded `major` do not hold. (a) The terminal draft state for workflow-touching managed PRs is the gate's tested, deliberate contract, not an unconsidered consumer fallout: mark-ready.test.mjs:262-278 names that exact population ("An `agent:managed` human PR is on this promote path and is not restricted from pushing workflows, so the gate has to refuse it") and asserts the PR stays a draft "for a human to review the workflow change" — judging that design is the security/design lens. (b) "Does not page" is the pre-existing exit-1 semantics for EVERY gate (agent-review-panel.yml:1531-1542: "exit 1 = a gate said no; the job succeeds and the PR stays a draft"); a missing AI disclosure or a red lens check behaved identically before this change, so gate 1b changes nothing about the paging contract. (c) The human is in fact informed and by the gate's own name: mark-ready.mjs:243-249 prints the per-gate ❌ report, the promote step cats it into the log (agent-review-panel.yml:1516), and the sticky loop-status note (agent-review-panel.yml:1577) says a ready gate was not satisfied and points at that step; the same comment is re-derived in full each update (:1242-1246), so the panel's ":1263 promotes once CI is green" line is superseded by the accurate promote note in the same run. (d) The "unbounded per-push panel cost" claim has a concrete counterexample: the panel-admission gate (agent-review-panel.yml:192-259) keys only on the agent/ prefix, the agent:managed label and the paged latch — there is no draft/ready check — so a PROMOTED PR re-runs the panel on every green push exactly as a gate-1b-blocked one does; the per-push cost is pre-existing and self-documented at :135-137, and gate 1b adds none of it. What remains is drift in two informational strings (agent-loop.yml:166, which is already hedged with "can promote it … a human approval is still required to merge", and agent-review-panel.yml:1263). Under this lens's rubric that is verbatim the `minor` bucket — "a doc, or comment left describing the old contract" — not a broken call site, bypass, or violated invariant, so it is not blocking.
